title: Two pointers and windows
summary: Solve pair, palindrome and subarray problems in one pass by moving indices instead of nesting loops.

questions.prompt: In a sorted array, find two numbers that add up to a target, using O(1) extra space. Which approach?
options: Two pointers from both ends, moving inward depending on the sum
A hash set of values seen so far

questions.prompt: Complete the line that slides a fixed window of size k one step to the right.
Move all zeros in an array to the end, keeping the other numbers in their original order, in place. Which approach?
options: A write pointer that copies each non-zero forward, then fills the rest with zeros
Copy the non-zeros into a new array
A hash map from value to count

questions.prompt: A variable-size sliding window finds the longest subarray with sum at most k. Why does it assume the numbers are non-negative?
options: With negatives, adding an element can lower the sum and removing one can raise it, so 'shrink while too big' no longer works
Java arrays can't hold negative numbers
Only fixed-size windows need non-negative numbers
